title: Vision Language Models as Values Detectors

live_model.evidence: "The models evaluated are gpt-4o-2024-05-13, llava-v1.6-34b-hf, llava-v1.6-mistral-7b-hf, llava-v1.6-vicuna-7b-hf, and llava-v1.6-vicuna-13b-hf."; Table 2 row 'GPT-4o', Average 0.33, SD 0.48.

prompt.location: Sec 3.1: "The prompt used is: 'Identify what is the element that needs attention in this image. If nothing is relevant answer with none.'"
prompt.note: Temperature 1, no system prompt, generation capped at 100 tokens, 3 completions per image.

claim.location: Table 2, row 'GPT-4o': Average 0.33, SD 0.48; 12 images x 3 completions = 36 generations (Sec 3.2)

data.source: 12 custom images depicting ambiguous/potentially sensitive everyday scenes with 14 human annotators (168 sentences); dataset release not confirmed in retrieved text

notes: GPT-4o is one of five vision-language models compared against 14 human annotators on identifying the salient element in ambiguous images; all models used the identical printed prompt. Model outputs were binary-scored by hand against the human-annotated 'most common element of focus', which is ordinary correctness grading rather than a human_outcome-style dependent variable.
